Platform Shoes
PLAT-form SHOOZ
noun (Boomer slang)
Platform (Middle French plate-forme, a flat form or raised level surface) + shoes. Shoes with a thick sole under the whole foot are ancient (the Greek tragic actor’s kothornos, the Venetian chopine of the 1500s), but platform shoes as a mass fashion for both men and women belong to the early-to-mid 1970s — glam rock stars such as Elton John and KISS, disco dancers, and teenagers everywhere teetered on soles several inches thick.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Platform shoes were the towering, thick-soled shoes and boots of the 1970s: men and women alike adding three, four, or six inches to their height, stars stomping across stages, teenagers wobbling to school. The Christian observation: the shoe is a joke about the oldest human wish — to be taller than we are. Our Lord made the same joke gently: "Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?" (Mat 6:27). The platform shoe was a way to add a few inches by money rather than thought, and it changed nothing that mattered. Scripture records a short man who handled his height better. Zacchaeus "sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature" (Luk 19:3); so he climbed a sycamore tree, forgot his dignity, and was met by the Lord. The lesson is that God is not impressed by elevation. "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me" (Jer 9:23–24). The glam stars on their platforms were displaying themselves; Zacchaeus up his tree was seeking Christ. Same impulse to get higher, opposite direction. A short boy needs to hear that God measured Saul’s height and chose David’s heart.

Webster 1828 Definition

1970s fashion (glam rock and disco) for shoes with thick soles several inches high — an old human wish to be taller that Our Lord gently mocked (Mat 6:27), set against Zacchaeus, little of stature, who climbed a tree to see Jesus (Luk 19:3).

PLATFORM SHOES, n. pl. (1970s; Boomer era) Shoes or boots with very thick soles, often several inches high, worn by both sexes. Also platforms.

Webster (1828) — PLATFORM, noun [plat, flat, form.] The sketch of any thing horizontally delineated; the ichnography. 1. A place laid out after any model. 2. In the military art, an elevation of earth or a floor of wood or stone, on which cannons are mounted to fire on an enemy.

Decode for families: platforms come back every twenty years. So does the wish behind them.

Key Scripture

Mat 6:27 — "Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?"

Luk 19:3 — "And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature."

Jer 9:23 — "Thus saith the LORD, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches:"

Jer 9:24 — "But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD."

1Sa 16:7 — "But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart."

Modern Corruption

Platform shoes bought stature with money and turned height into display; Scripture mocks the effort to add a cubit and shows a short man seeking Christ, not elevation.

expand to see more

The platform shoe was vanity with a sense of humor. Rock stars wore them to tower over the crowd; ordinary people wore them to be noticed. Nobody was fooled about anyone’s real height. The comedy is the comedy of all self-elevation: everyone can see the soles. Jeremiah’s list of false glories — wisdom, might, riches — could have included inches (Jer 9:23).

The gospel does not make short men tall; it makes small men great. Zacchaeus was a small man in every sense — short, despised, a tax collector — and Christ stopped under his tree and called him by name. The God who "looketh on the heart" (1Sa 16:7) does not need anyone to stand on a platform to be seen.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Middle French plate-forme (a flat form, a ground plan) → English platform (a raised flat surface) + shoes → 1970s platform shoes.

Middle French plate-forme — a plan, a flat surface; Old French plat, flat

Greek kothornos — the high-soled boot of tragic actors

16th c. Venice: chopines, platform overshoes several inches high

Early-to-mid 1970s: glam rock and disco make platform shoes a mass fashion

Greek hēlikia — stature (Mat 6:27; Luk 19:3)
